comment: Datasets the quality benchmark downloads at run time. Nothing here is committed to the repository: each entry names the publisher's own URL, the SHA-256 and exact byte count of every download, and the reference products. A file whose bytes, hash and licence are not all recorded does not belong here. See DATASETS.md for why each was chosen and what was rejected.

aerial-nadir.title: Bandamaji, Grande Comore (Comoros) drone survey, 2023-06-26

licence.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
licence.redistribution: allowed with attribution; this benchmark downloads only

reference_files.publisher_settings: OpenDroneMap: orthophoto-resolution=1 cm, dem-resolution=2.0 cm, dsm=true, auto-boundary=true

aerial-nadir.notes: The publisher states OpenDroneMap reconstructed 102 of 102 images at a 2.4 cm GSD over 0.048 km^2. Its ortho and DSM are both at 2.19 cm/px (the record quotes 1 and 2.0, which OpenDroneMap reads in centimetres), so the reference matches the imagery resolution rather than being coarser than it.
aerial-nadir.param_overrides_reason: Four measured limits, each with the run that found it. (1) 30 of 102 images: the full set at 20 MP spent over five hours in BuildDepthMaps. (2) MatchPhotos keypoint_limit_per_mpx=250: at the default 1000 the matching was killed out of memory at 97%. (3) BuildDepthMaps downscale=8: quarters the depth-map pixel count, leaving a 1.7 cm grid still finer than the 2.4 cm GSD the imagery justifies. (4) BuildOrthomosaic resolution=0.10 with refine_seamlines=false: the site is 0.048 km2, so 2.4 cm is 83 million cells and even 5 cm is 19 million, each cell carrying an alpha-expansion over 30 camera labels - both overran the stage budget. 10 cm is 4.8 million cells and a normal ortho deliverable, and the argmax seam labelling keeps the cost linear in cells; the trade is visible seams where the score steps, which the side-by-side comparison shows. The effective-resolution metric is measured against the mosaic's own 10 cm cell and the blur is read from a full-resolution window, so 'did the mosaic get softer' stays a valid signal at any requested resolution. All four are recorded in every metrics JSON and printed in the report.
aerial-nadir.max_images_reason: The dense stage costs images x pixels, and 102 frames at 20 MP does not fit a weekly job on a shared CPU runner: the first run of this benchmark spent over five hours in BuildDepthMaps and was cancelled. 30 images is the block of 30 nearest the flight's centre by GPS (the median position of the set), which is a compact spatial cluster with the overlap the stereo stage needs — a strided sample across the whole flight would only just overlap and would produce sparse depth maps for a reason that has nothing to do with the code. The cluster is chosen deterministically and every selected file name is printed in the run log and listed in the report.

terrestrial-laser.title: ETH3D high-res multi-view training scene 'terrains'
terrestrial-laser.publisher: ETH Zurich, Computer Vision and Geometry Group (Schops et al., CVPR 2017)
terrestrial-laser.flight: oblique handheld DSLR (ground-truth geometry reference, not a drone flight)

licence.name: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International
licence.redistribution: not allowed; the benchmark downloads inside the CI job only and never commits or publishes the data

terrestrial-laser.notes: The scan_eval archive holds the laser scan already aligned into the image frame, which is why it is used instead of the 1.9 GB full ground-truth bundle. The reconstruction is registered onto the scan by similarity ICP before scoring, because an SfM model has no metric scale and these images carry no GPS. ETH3D scores accuracy and completeness at 2/5/10 cm; this benchmark uses the same tolerances.
terrestrial-laser.param_overrides_reason: The same keypoint and depth-map budgets as the aerial set, for the same measured reason: at 24 MP per frame the default keypoint density killed the match stage out of memory. There is no ortho resolution override here — this dataset's reference is a laser cloud, and BuildOrthomosaic is only measured reference-free.
terrestrial-laser.max_images_reason: 42 frames at 24 MP is 64 million depth-map pixels at downscale 8 over 42 views, which does not fit the weekly budget on a shared CPU runner. 30 of the 42 is enough for a 30-view dense reconstruction of the scene while leaving headroom; the selection is the 30 images nearest the set's median position (file order for these frames, which carry no GPS), deterministic, and every selected file name is listed in the report.

gcp-rtk.title: Helenenschacht RTK sample, Autel Evo II Pro RTK (OpenDroneMap)

licence.name: GNU General Public License 3.0
licence.redistribution: download and measure only; never redistributed

gcp-rtk.param_overrides_reason: keypoint_limit_per_mpx=500 (~10000 keypoints per 20 MP image) was measured best on this block with the match_params experiments: 250 aligned 146 of 176 cameras at 5.31 cm horizontal check RMS in 12342 s, 500 aligned 169 at 4.36 cm in 5924 s, and 1000 aligned 174 at 4.47 cm in 14980 s. 500 is the most accurate and the fastest of the three. Reference preselection (GPS neighbours) caps the match work at ~20 pairs per camera. The GCP validation never runs the dense stage.
gcp-rtk.notes: 35 image observations of 5 surveyed GCPs (ODM gcp_list format, header EPSG:4326) and a 5-point CSV (Name;Easting;Northing;Elevation;Longitude;Latitude) surveyed with an Emlid Reach RS2 via NTRIP at a stated 1-2 cm accuracy. Every image's XMP carries RtkFlag 50 (fixed) and RtkStdLon/Lat/Hgt, and RTK_Data/101FTASK_Timestamp.mrk carries the same per-exposure antenna positions, deviations and the GPS event time; the benchmark runs the protocol with --camera-accuracy per-image, so each camera is weighted by its own solution, and uses the event-mark log for the timing comparison. Photographs by Daniel Dobosi, published by OpenDroneMap under GPL-3.0.

gcp-eurosdr.title: Wards Hill quarry, Northumberland, UK (EuroSDR RPAS benchmark, DJI P4 RTK)
gcp-eurosdr.publisher: Zenodo record 10059050 (Newcastle University Geospatial Engineering for EuroSDR)

licence.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
licence.redistribution: allowed with attribution; the imagery is downloaded and measured, never redistributed, and the committed observations are our own derived data

gcp-eurosdr.param_overrides_reason: keypoint_limit_per_mpx=250 is the density the aerial-nadir and terrestrial-laser datasets use and what fits a 16 GB runner: 430 images at 500 is 2.4x the gcp-rtk block's keypoint load, which killed the measurement runner out of memory on its first attempt. Reference preselection (GPS neighbours) caps the match work at ~20 pairs per camera. The GCP validation never runs the dense stage.
gcp-eurosdr.notes: The publisher ships the surveyed coordinates of 8 GCPs and 51 check points but NOT the pixel observations of their printed targets, so the benchmark measures them itself in a CI-only workflow (eurosdr-observations.yml) and commits the accepted observations as our own derived data under tools/bench/data/eurosdr/ (CC BY 4.0, Mills et al. 2023, Newcastle University / EuroSDR). The targets are 300 mm circular Perspex disks with a 100 mm black centre (white for check points, yellow for GCPs) on stakes 0.15-0.45 m above ground; the P4 RTK flew at 55 m AGL with an 8.8 mm lens and 2.41 um pixels, so the GSD is ~1.5 cm. The coordinates come from GCPsandCPs_coords.xlsx in ETRS89 geodetic lat/lon with ELLIPSOIDAL height on GRS80, so --gcp-height ellipsoidal applies directly and no geoid model is needed. The xlsx is the authoritative label source: the Phase3 text file's labels are shifted by one against it and are never read. The committed gcp_list is the GCP-only list (the eight GCPs) because the protocol does leave-one-out over every point in the list; the full 59-station list is kept alongside it as the complete derived data. The whole 430-image flight is used: a strided subset was tried and rejected, because taking every fourth frame halves the forward overlap and only 23 of 108 cameras registered. The block is aligned RTK-first (align_from_reference): AlignCameras' single global similarity fit keeps only 6 of 430 cameras inside its inlier threshold on this flight, so the block registers a small fraction of its images; placing each camera from its own RTK position and gimbal attitude registers all 430.
